touches.text: The launcher is Python (bin/cairn), run by Cairn's own interpreter, so Windows needs no bash. Typing `cairn` works on either platform.

Each platform shell does two things, in order, before handing over: it elevates, then it runs Cairn's own Python on the launcher (on Windows `@python <path>\cairn ...`; on Linux the same without the @). Every decision after that is Python's; the shell holds no other logic beyond the fall-over above.

Elevation is the shell's, settled before Python starts, and nothing inside asks again. On Windows the shell runs in an elevated PowerShell. On Linux the shell sudoes the launch, with IS_SANDBOX=1 set so Claude Code accepts bypass permissions under root. WHY: the whole box is the sandbox, so elevating once at launch is simpler than elevating on request; IS_SANDBOX=1 is set on every box for that reason. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator

Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).

What Rescue fixes by hand, it turns into a step in that platform's deterministic installer, so next time the installer handles it alone. Each rescue makes the next one less likely: the system keeps learning.
Owns the CC launcher (superclaude): starts Claude Code with Cairn's session contract, in its own memory-capped cgroup. WHY: Claude can OOM the box.

superclaude is Python on every box, launched by the platform shell (5.4.3.8.5), and inherits the elevation the shell settled (5.4.3.8.6): elevated PowerShell on Windows, sudo with IS_SANDBOX=1 on Linux; it never elevates itself. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.

In front of it sits a thin platform shell (a shell script on Linux, cairn.cmd or cairn.ps1 on Windows) with enough brains to fall over to Rescue (6.5) when it can't find Cairn's Python, or Python throws, or anything else stops the launcher. The failure throws a trouble ticket (3.4.3), and the ticket is Rescue's "read this" (6.5.3.5); a repeat increments that ticket's counter. Rescue's prompt says: at the end of proving the fix, check for more errors, to clear or fix as appropriate. WHY: trouble has to be able to report when nothing else can (2.3.7.1.3).
On a new platform a simple cairn.bat comes first: at the start it takes only the rescueclaude option, launching Claude with 200K context and dangerous permissions.

System: a box has to name itself before any bus is up (a saveslate, an install), so the system device publishes the host's name and OS family (6.6.3.7). - akiendelllinux_cc_0 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):

The hostname comes from the system device. It answers which box (the short hostname, lowercased) and which OS family, and nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname. Callers reach it through the client tool it publishes (2.3.7.1.5), so a box names itself on every OS, Windows included, with no bus running. - akiendelllinux_cc_0
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.
